brief: Strong US growth data and rising energy costs pushed the market to price a faster Fed tightening pace: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.16%, its highest since 2007, the 30-year hit its highest since 2004, and October hike odds rose from 53% to 64%, alongside a flash composite PMI at 58.4 (highest since July 2021) with input costs rising at the fastest pace in nearly four years. UBS's own view diverges from the market: it forecasts only one further 25bp hike, in December, expecting underlying inflation to stay moderate, a shallower path than markets are pricing. Higher energy costs remain a risk to growth via reduced household purchasing power and higher company costs, but UBS expects resilient growth and earnings (S&P 500 forecast: 25% growth in 2026, 14% in 2027) to let equities absorb higher yields. UBS recommends positioning for further equity gains with diversification and reduced single-stock concentration, rates fixed income Attractive, favors medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds and investment-grade credit, and stays cautious on the longest maturities and lower-quality credit.
